findings.claim: The app and reader pools still authenticate as the postgres superuser and only assume role_app_backend through the startup role GUC, so session_user remains a superuser for the whole connection lifetime. RLS is genuinely enforced today because current_user is role_app_backend (NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS) and no request-path code resets it (verified: @stynx-nyx/data pools.js passes connectionString straight to pg.Pool, database.js only issues transaction-local set_config, the single SET ROLE occurrence is in migration-runner.js on the owner path, and pg-pool issues no DISCARD ALL). The residual gap is that any future RESET ROLE, SET ROLE postgres, pool-level DISCARD ALL or superuser-owned SECURITY DEFINER path would restore bypass, and this configuration approximates rather than reproduces docs/meta/pec-external-environment-contract.md lines 46-51, which requires distinct owner/app/reader identities with neither superuser nor BYPASSRLS on the reader.
findings.fix: Create dedicated LOGIN roles detran_app and detran_reader granted into role_app_backend during backend:db:reset and point STYNX_APP_DATABASE_URL and STYNX_READER_DATABASE_URL at those principals, keeping postgres only for STYNX_OWNER_DATABASE_URL, DATABASE_URL and DETRAN_TEST_DATABASE_URL.

findings.claim: The cross-tenant sensor asserts only absence (toEqual([])), so it distinguishes an RLS bypass from enforcement but cannot distinguish enforcement from a listing that returns empty for an unrelated reason, such as a broken query, a missing grant or a tenant context that resolves to null. The correction did not weaken this assertion, it was already the shape that detected the PR #40 failure, but its discriminating power in the passing direction is untested.
findings.fix: Seed one ops.agency_unit row under localTenantId in beforeAll and assert the response contains exactly that row, keeping the cross-tenant fixture excluded, so the test fails both on bypass and on an empty-for-the-wrong-reason listing.

Configuration validity confirmed against the installed stack: pg-connection-string 2.14.0 copies unknown query params from result.searchParams into the config object with percent-decoding applied, and the encoded string contains no literal space and no sequence matching its re-encoding guard, so options resolves to the literal '-c role=role_app_backend'. pg 8.23.0 reads options in connection-parameters.js:83 and emits it in the startup packet in client.js:567-568. role is a PGC_USERSET GUC, so the superuser session assumes role_app_backend at connection start.

RLS enforcement under that role is real: 01-schemas.sql:15 creates role_app_backend NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS, auth.create_rls_policy (11-auth-functions.sql:54-58) applies ENABLE plus FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY with tenant_id = auth.current_tenant(), and tables are owned by postgres, not by the current role, so policies apply on every app and reader statement.

The tenant channel still works under the non-superuser role: @stynx-nyx/data database.js:168-181 sets app.role, app.tenant_id, app.actor_id and app.request_id via transaction-local set_config, and auth.current_tenant() reads app.tenant_id. The REVOKE of auth.set_current_tenant from role_app_backend (20-rls-policies.sql:33) is not on this path. The e2e fixture insert runs on a separate superuser client with app.role=owner, which is the intended owner-side seeding path and is cleaned up in afterAll.
Step ordering in backend-kernel is safe: backend:db:reset creates role_app_backend before any step that opens an app or reader pool, so the startup role assignment cannot fail on a missing role.

No cross-step contamination: the only consumers of STYNX_OWNER/APP/READER_DATABASE_URL are backend/app/src/detran-runtime.ts, its spec, backend/app/tests/e2e/runtime-profiles.e2e.spec.ts, backend/app/README.md, docs and round files. The senatran adapter contract step and the ops-parameter and inf-ait tiers do not read these variables.
